scenarios.label: 1 intermittent API, no database (360 req/day, 90 spaced windows)
scenarios.description: One 256 MB API answering 90 spaced 4-request windows/day (10,800 req/mo) with long idle gaps between windows, grounded in the measured spread FastAPI trace (7 billed awake seconds per window = 5.25 h/mo, 1.353515625 GB-RAM-h).

scenarios.label: 1 evenly distributed 24/7 API + Postgres (1 req / 30 s)
scenarios.description: One 512 MB production API receiving 1 request every 30 seconds all month (87,600 req/mo) plus one managed PostgreSQL database. Minute-scale sleep timers never trigger, while Gregale pauses ~1-2 s after each request.

scenarios.label: 5 evenly distributed 24/7 services + Postgres (1 req / 30 s each)
scenarios.description: Five 512 MB backend services (public API, webhook receiver, admin API, worker API, MCP server) each receiving 1 request every 30 seconds around the clock (438,000 req/mo total) sharing one managed PostgreSQL database.

scenarios.label: 1 continuously busy 24/7 API + Postgres (2 req/s, no idle gaps)
scenarios.description: One 512 MB production API serving 2 requests/second continuously all month (5,256,000 req/mo) with one managed PostgreSQL database. Traffic arrives faster than Gregale's pause threshold, so all platforms bill 730 hours.
